stemMd: Which substance can form an amide bond by reacting through its carboxyl group with an amine?

options.label: A
options.textMd: An alkane with no functional group

explanationMd: An amide linkage connects a carbonyl carbon to nitrogen. It can be formed from a carboxylic-acid derivative and an amine under suitable conditions. Peptide bonds are amide bonds formed between amino-acid carboxyl and amino groups.

distractorRationale.a: It lacks the carboxyl group needed for the described linkage.
distractorRationale.c: It has no organic carboxyl functionality.
distractorRationale.e: An ionic salt does not supply an acyl group for an amide bond.
distractorRationale.d: Nitrogen gas does not contain a carboxyl group.
